name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS)
summary: CMCHIS provides cashless health insurance cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for treatment at government and empanelled private hospitals, including surgeries, implants and follow-up care. Eligibility: families with annual income below ₹1,20,000 holding a ration card. Over 1,000 medical procedures are covered across empanelled hospitals throughout Tamil Nadu. Apply or check eligibility at cmchistn.com or the nearest government hospital.
verificationNote: Procedure count and empanelled-hospital count could not be confirmed against the official portal (JavaScript-rendered). Secondary sources disagree: 1,016 vs 1,416 vs 2,053 procedures. Summary deliberately says 'over 1,000' until a headless-browser crawl or manual check confirms the exact figure. Income limit corrected from the stale ₹72,000 to ₹1,20,000.

name: Innuyir Kaappom – Nammai Kaakkum 48 (Road Accident Emergency Care)
summary: Any road accident victim in Tamil Nadu receives completely free emergency treatment for the first 48 hours after the accident, up to ₹2 lakh, covering 81 critical treatments. The State Health Department bears the cost. No ration card or income limit applies — people not eligible for CMCHIS, and visitors from other states and countries, are also covered. Around 721 hospitals (248 government and 473 private) are empanelled. A ₹5,000 reward is given to any person who brings an accident victim to hospital within the first 48 hours.

name: Dr. Kalaignar Insurance Scheme for Life Saving Treatments
summary: The Dr. Kalaignar Insurance Scheme covers life-saving treatments for cancer, heart disease, kidney failure and organ transplants up to ₹5 lakh. Beneficiaries are ration card holders not covered under CMCHIS. Treatment is available at empanelled private and government hospitals.

name: Tamil Nadu Free Medicine Scheme
summary: All government hospitals in Tamil Nadu provide free essential medicines to outpatients and inpatients. Over 600 essential drugs are available free of cost through the Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation (TNMSC). Patients need only a prescription from the government doctor.

name: Free Dialysis Programme
summary: The Tamil Nadu government provides free dialysis to kidney failure patients at 175+ government hospitals and Primary Health Centres, delivered under the National Dialysis Programme. Patients requiring regular dialysis can register at their nearest government hospital. Both haemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis are covered.

name: Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam (Doorstep Healthcare)
summary: Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam, launched in 2021, sends healthcare teams of doctors, nurses and health workers to homes across Tamil Nadu for doorstep screening of 27 diseases and conditions including diabetes, hypertension, TB, cancer and mental health. Free medicines are delivered on the spot, and over 3.5 crore households have been covered. Beneficiaries receive follow-up referrals to PHCs or government hospitals.

name: Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy Maternity Benefit Scheme
summary: Pregnant women in Tamil Nadu receive ₹18,000 in maternity benefit — ₹14,000 as cash assistance in three instalments plus two nutrition kits worth ₹4,000. Eligibility: women aged 18–55 from BPL families, and also those holding E-Shram or MGNREGA job cards or belonging to SC/ST communities. The benefit applies to the first two deliveries only, and post-delivery instalments require the birth to take place in a government or approved private facility. Register through the PICME portal or the nearest government hospital or health sub-centre.

name: Cradle Baby Scheme
summary: Under the Cradle Baby Scheme, parents can anonymously place unwanted babies — most often girl babies — in cradles placed at government hospitals and child welfare centres. The child is then placed for adoption through legal procedures. The scheme exists to prevent female infanticide and abandonment.

name: Free Cancer Screening Programme
summary: Tamil Nadu offers free screening for cervical, breast and oral cancers at government hospitals and PHCs under the national NCD programme (NPCDCS). Early detection tests are done free of cost. Patients diagnosed with cancer are referred to government oncology centres for free treatment under CMCHIS.

name: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme (Pudhumai Penn)
tamilName: மூவலூர் ராமாமிர்தம் அம்மையார் உயர்கல்வி உறுதித் திட்டம் (புதுமைப் பெண்)
summary: Girl students who studied Class 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government or government-aided schools receive ₹1,000 per month, credited directly to their bank account, for the full duration of their first higher education course (UG degree, diploma or ITI). There is no income ceiling. Launched on 18 March 2022. Register through the college or at pudhumaipenn.tn.gov.in.

name: Tamil Pudhalvan Scheme
summary: Tamil Pudhalvan is the counterpart of Pudhumai Penn for boys. Male students who studied Class 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government or government-aided schools receive ₹1,000 per month for the duration of their higher education course (UG degree, diploma, polytechnic or ITI). Students from private schools are not eligible. Launched on 9 August 2024, it covers over 3 lakh students. Apply online through the University Management Information System (UMIS) portal at umis.tn.gov.in.

name: Free Uniform, Books and School Supplies Scheme
tamilName: இலவச சீருடை, புத்தகம் மற்றும் பள்ளி பொருட்கள் திட்டம்
summary: All students enrolled in Tamil Nadu government schools receive free uniforms (4 sets), textbooks, notebooks, a schoolbag, geometry box, colour pencils and atlas. These are distributed at the start of every academic year through the school. No application is needed — it is automatic for enrolled students.

name: Chief Minister's Nutritious Meal Programme (Mid-Day Meal)
summary: All students in government and government-aided schools receive a free nutritious lunch on school days. The meal includes rice, sambar, vegetables, egg (three times a week) and milk. It operates in over 50,000 schools benefiting around 30 lakh students across Tamil Nadu.

name: Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme
summary: The Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme provides a free hot breakfast on every school working day to primary school children in Classes 1 to 5 in government and government-aided schools. Launched on 15 September 2022 in Madurai, it has since expanded statewide to roughly 31,000 schools serving about 18.5 lakh students. The rotating menu includes upma, kitchadi, pongal and sweet dishes, with millet-based breakfasts at least twice a week, providing around 293 calories and 9.85 g of protein per child per meal. No application is needed.

name: SC/ST Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarships
tamilName: தாழ்த்தப்பட்டோர் / பழங்குடியினர் தொடக்க, இடைநிலை மற்றும் உயர்கல்வி உதவித்தொகை
summary: SC/ST students receive pre-matric scholarships (Class 1–10) and post-matric scholarships (Class 11 onwards, including college and research level) covering tuition fees, hostel charges and a monthly stipend. The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department additionally provides free education up to Class 12, public examination fee assistance for Class 10 and 12, subject-wise cash incentives, hostel accommodation with special guides, and a book bank for professional courses. Apply through the Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Welfare Department before the academic year deadline.

name: OBC / MBC Scholarships (BC, MBC & Minorities Welfare)
summary: The BC, MBC & Minorities Welfare Department offers pre-matric and post-matric scholarships (Class 11 to research level), a Free Education Scheme, and free-education scholarships specifically for three-year diploma/polytechnic courses and for professional courses including engineering, medicine, agriculture, veterinary science and law. District- and state-level prizes are also awarded for Class 10 and 12 performance. Apply through the department portal with a caste certificate and income certificate.

name: First Generation Graduate Scholarship
summary: Students who are the first in their family to pursue higher education (degree or diploma) receive the First Generation Graduate Scholarship — ₹1,500 per year for degree students and ₹1,125 for diploma students. First-generation students entering engineering through the TNEA government quota also receive a tuition fee concession. Apply at the college with a declaration that no parent holds a degree.

name: Free Laptop Scheme for Government School Students
summary: Students who pass Class 10 from Tamil Nadu government schools and join Class 11 in government schools receive a free laptop, distributed through the school at the start of Class 11. The scheme aims to bridge the digital divide.

name: Minority Community Scholarship
summary: Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain and Parsi students whose family income is below ₹2 lakh per year can apply for minority pre-matric and post-matric scholarships. Apply through the Tamil Nadu BC, MBC & Minorities Welfare Department, or through the National Scholarship Portal for the centrally funded components.

name: Free Education in Government Engineering and Arts Colleges
tamilName: அரசு பொறியியல் மற்றும் கலை அறிவியல் கல்லூரிகளில் இலவச கல்வி
summary: The Tamil Nadu government provides free education (full tuition fee waiver) for students from families earning below ₹2.5 lakh per year in all government arts, science, engineering and polytechnic colleges. Students from all communities are eligible. Apply through the college at the time of admission with an income certificate.
